title: PCP capabilities
description: What a connector (or one room of it) can do. Modules check these, never platform names. Declared in hello; a room.joined event may carry a narrower set for that room.

events.description: Event types this connector may emit.

actions.description: Action types this connector executes. Anything else is answered with error code 'unsupported'.

features.description: Finer-grained flags. Unknown flags are ignored.

message_ids.description: Platform gives stable message ids (needed for reply_to, react, quote).

content_elements.description: Outbound element types the connector renders natively; others are flattened to text.

private_messages.description: room = PMs travel through a room (Camfrog); global = DM channels (Discord); none.

display_markup.description: Display names may carry markup (see UserRef.display_raw).

user_id_kind.description: What UserRef.id is on this platform.

self_state_observable.description: Whether the connector can observe its own mic state, rather than inferring it from its own commands.

sticker_send_ack.description: always | sometimes | never: whether sticker.send can confirm posting. Camfrog acks only on some room servers.

platform_commands.description: Commands platform.command accepts (e.g. Camfrog slash commands).

message_id_scope.description: (1.1) How long message ids stay valid: stable (durable platform ids), session (unique only within one connector session, e.g. cf-m-<session>-<room>-<seq>), none. Replaces the 1.0 boolean message_ids for 1.1 receivers; a 1.0 connector's message_ids=true means stable, false means none. A connector whose scope is session or none sends message_ids=false.

edits_own.description: (1.1) The bot can edit its own messages (message.edit).

deletes.description: (1.1) What message.delete can remove: own (the bot's own messages), any (needs moderator rights), none.

delete_window_s.description: (1.1) Messages older than this cannot be deleted (Telegram: 172800). Absent = no limit.

reply_refs.description: (1.1) send.reply_to and relay.reply_to_remote produce native replies.

masquerade.description: (1.1) Relayed lines can carry the author's name and avatar natively (Discord webhooks) instead of a text prefix.

relay_prefix.description: (1.1) Relayed lines are rendered with a text prefix ({name} and a tag).

reactions_custom.description: (1.1) Custom (non-unicode) emoji can be used in reactions.

reactions_durable.description: (1.1) The connector can report reactions per user as normal-priority message.reaction events. It sends them in place of 1.0's low-priority reaction only when welcome.subscribe lists message.reaction and not reaction; otherwise it keeps sending reaction (spec/PCP.md, Version negotiation).

components.description: (1.1) The connector renders card and actions elements natively (buttons, selects).

interactions.description: (1.1) The connector emits interaction events and executes interaction.defer/respond/followup.

privacy_edge_filter.description: (1.1) The connector applies the privacy edge filter of spec/PCP.md, Security and privacy: it drops lines, stickers, transcripts and turn audio of hidden or opted-out identities before anything is logged, and reports them only as anonymous presence. Absent = false.

inline_max_bytes.description: Largest attachment the connector posts natively; bigger media goes as a link.

pacing.description: (1.1) The platform's send limits, so a hub that paces relayed lines can do so without the connector re-ordering. Durations in ms; *_burst are line counts within the matching window.

gap_ms.description: Minimum gap between two lines of one sender.

room_gap_ms.description: Minimum gap between two lines in one room.

global_gap_ms.description: Minimum gap between any two lines of the connector's account.

dup_window_ms.description: The platform drops a line identical to one sent within this window.

features.$comment: (1.1) message_ids=true means stable ids to a 1.0 reader, so it never goes with a session or none scope.

message_max_bytes.description: (1.1) Line limit in UTF-8 bytes, for platforms that count bytes (IRC).
